core_claim.P: A user redeems tokens or swaps to base assets with the recipient address set to the Covenant contract itself (address(this)), and the base token's ERC20 transfer treats self-transfer as a no-op.
core_claim.I: Base token payouts in redeem() and swap() must not allow the recipient to be the contract itself, so that internal accounting (baseSupply) stays consistent with actual token balances and liquidity is not impaired.
core_claim.V: Self-transfer payouts decrement baseSupply without moving tokens, permanently locking base tokens in the contract and reducing effective liquidity for all users.

direct_impacts.description: Base tokens become permanently stranded/locked in the contract because they are not reflected in internal accounting and cannot be withdrawn through normal user flows or protocol fee collection.
direct_impacts.evidence_quote: These excess tokens become permanently stranded since they are not reflected in the internal accounting and cannot be withdrawn through normal user flows or protocol fee collection mechanisms.

direct_impacts.description: Effective liquidity available to all users is reduced because liquidity calculations rely on baseSupply rather than the actual token balance.
direct_impacts.evidence_quote: The locked funds reduce the effective liquidity available to all users, as liquidity calculations rely on baseSupply rather than the actual token balance

direct_impacts.description: Future redemptions may be impaired and overall market functionality degraded.
direct_impacts.evidence_quote: potentially impairing future redemptions and degrading overall market functionality
